This is such an important topic. Healthcare price transparency does not exist. 

Always challenge your healthcare bill by asking for an itemized report of the charges and in network allowable. 

If out of network, call the clinic or physician group and ask to negotiate a fair and reasonable payment. 

The insurance companies don’t pay their contractually required payments to physicians or ASCs forcing physicians and surgical centers to go out of network. 

Patients are balanced billed because insurance determines that the payment should be $0.01. 

Clinic and facility claims are submitted to the Independent Dispute Resolution process of the NSA act. We win over 90% of the time. 

Insurance companies ignore the win in arbitration and refuse to pay. There reason for not paying:  “the IDR determination is unenforceable, so we don’t need to pay.” 

Physicians sue insurance company to force them to pay. Insurance company loses in court and still refuses to pay IDR win. 

Insurance company appeals loss in court. Circuit court judge says insurance company needs to pay.  Insurance company refuses to pay. 

Insurance company appeals again.  And the saga goes on for years. 

We acted in good faith receiving no payment while insurance profited from our good will.  The patients are left wondering why the bills are so high. 

I am happy to send an itemized bill. 

The hospital never wants you to see their itemized bill. 

Question every insurance and hospital statement. 

The corruption runs deep. 

WE ARE SO TIRED OF THEIR SHENANIGANS.

@HealthGovInst Our ASC received a $0.01 payment for a $60,000 case. I sent it to our US senator.  

We MUST track initial payments vs QPA vs IDR award. 

Their brazen belligerent violations of the QPA requirements of the NSA are astounding. 

The must be held accountable.

Insurance payments equivalent to what I pay my pet groomer are repugnant. 

We frequently see payments of a few hundred dollars for major operations for facility claims at our ASC and even lower professionally. 

We received a payment of $0.01 for an ASC facility payment on a major case that typically reimburses at $60k or more.   

It’s a 🖕to every physician in private practice. 

When we appeal the underpayment, it’s denied. 

When we submit to the IDR, we win every time. 

They have no justification for their payments. They offer none to the arbitrator. 

These are RICO violations.  

The insurers are purposely paying way below Medicare fee schedules to force practices into unreasonable contracts or to submit to IDR. 

Our only recourse is the IDR or bill the patients. 

They then refuse to pay IDR wins.  They blame physicians and MSOs for price gouging. 

They lie, steal, and blame greedy doctors. 

A Blue Cross attorney recently argued in court:  “the IDR determination is as good as writing an IOU on a napkin to your mother”.

Insurers are operating in bad faith by agreeing to participate in the IDR process and then not paying when they lose. 

They litigate in court when they lose. 

All we are asking for is fair and reasonable payments.

I can make these claims because I am the medical director of a medical weight loss clinic and I have 30 years experience and am board certified in this specialty. I have authored peer reviewed clinical and scientific papers.  I have been involved in multiple clinical trials. I am a key opinion leader in metabolism and treatment of obesity. 

After thousands of scripts written with our medical providers, we haven’t seen any permanent GI injury. 

Claims of gastroparesis are very unlikely to be true. Gastroparesis is an idiopathic disease. GI peristalsis is slowed by GLP-1s, but its dose dependent and resolves once the medication is stopped. 

Any medication will have side effects, but with GLPs the GI distress resolves once the medication is stopped or the dose is reduced. In regard to other conditions, many of these patients have medical conditions, especially cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Some of these patient’s metabolic problems are undiagnosed until there’s a problem. Just because it’s associated, doesn’t meant it’s causal. 

GLP-1s are anti inflammatory drugs that bind to activated T cells. They reduce systemic inflammation including arthritis, MASH, dermatitis, and coronary artery disease.  Obesity is a chronic inflammatory disease closely linked to insulin resistance. Insulin resistance goes into remission with these medications. Ali g with their prediabetes. Those who have type 2 diabetes, have had insulin resistance for over decades. 

There’s a lot of fat shaming on social media regarding these drugs. These are the first weight loss medications that have  incredible efficacy that appears to be durable.  

GLP-1s must be Rx under medical supervision in a program that focuses on lifestyle changes.  Without that they will lose lean mass and can rapidly regain weight once they stop. 

We have weaned many patients off GLPs as long as it’s used as a tool.
